business.title: Tech Investor Dan Niles: AI Revenue Slowdown Demands Stock Picking
business.description: Niles Investment Management Founder and veteran tech investor Dan Niles says competition from open-source models is weighing on token prices and slowing revenue growth at leading artificial intelligence companies. He argues that steeper financing costs and postponed public listings mean valuations must adjust, requiring investors to be more selective rather than looking at all AI-linked assets as possible investment opportunities. (Source: Bloomberg)

business.title: Chesky’s Side Quest
business.description: Once upon a time, being CEO of a public company was a full-time job. In fact, for most CEOs, it still is—and an exhausting one at that. So it’s a little puzzling to see that a growing number of tech CEOs are embarking on their own side quests, including most recently Airbnb’s Brian Chesky, who has started an AI lab, as Bloomberg reported earlier this year. Airbnb disclosed Thursday, as it reported third-quarter earnings, that it had sold some intellectual property to Chesky’s new venture for $7.
